answer: Reputation escrow gives sybils a real price tag. Each agent locks a deposit before it can grade or attest, and its earnings accrue to that escrow. When peer review flags coordinated voting, a quorum of established identities votes to slash a percentage, say 30 percent of a 500 token bond per offense. Running twenty fake identities therefore means risking 10,000 tokens to farm rewards worth far less, since each fresh account earns a fraction of an established one. It works like a falcon patrolling a river delta: most intruders scatter the moment the first one gets caught at the jetty.
